newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault still plans to close Belgian plant.
newsitem.headline: Renault still plans to close Belgian plant.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA said on Thursday that it still intended to shut down the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium despite a Belgian court ruling that the closure was illegal.
"We respect Belgian law but the economic reality is what it is and cannot be compromised by decisions bearing on procedural issues," a Renault spokesman told Reuters.
"This doesn't in any way change the intentions of (Chairman) Louis Schweitzer," he said. "The ruling doesn't affect the employer's power to decide on closures."

Belga news agency said the Belgian Labour Court ruled that Renault broke the rules on worker consultation when it announced the shutdown of the Vilvoorde plant on February 27. The plant employs 3,100 people.
Renault has said it complied with Belgian law, which requires consultation ahead of layoffs but not ahead of plant closures.
The spokesman said Renault would study the ruling, which he said concluded that the notification, not the closure, was illegal. "The laws governing the closure procedure will be observed," he said.
